name: render
summary: Turns a template.Doc into the files a report is configured for — PDF, Excel (.xlsx), CSV — entirely in memory as Artifacts (bytes + filename + content type), never paths. Formats are a pluggable registry.
exposes: Renderer interface: Extension() string, ContentType() string, Render(template.Doc) ([]byte, error)
Render(doc, format, name) (Artifact, error) and RenderAll(doc, formats, name) ([]Artifact, error)
key_notes: Adding a format = one new file implementing Renderer + one entry in the `renderers` slice in render.go. Nothing outside this package names a format except the user's stored configuration.

The `renderers` slice order IS the canonical order: ParseFormats dedupes and re-sorts into it, so a report's formats are stored and displayed consistently however the client listed them. It's also why Formats[0] is a safe default for the download endpoint.

The PDF is DRAWN from the Doc blocks with fpdf, not converted from the template's HTML — deliberately, to avoid shipping a headless browser. If you change a template's HTML you must change its Document() too or the formats diverge.
PDF uses the Helvetica core font (nothing embedded, small files), A4 in millimetres, and samples at most widthSampleRows = 200 rows to size columns.

The CSV starts with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel doesn't fall back to the ANSI code page, and writes numbers UNFORMATTED (no thousands separators) because a CSV is usually read by another program. Its records are intentionally ragged — that's the cost of flattening a document into a sheet.
XLSX writes real numbers wherever template.Value.IsNumber, so recipients can sort/filter/sum. The sheet is always named 'Report' (Excel's 31-char + punctuation limits vs. user-supplied report names).

Filename() slugifies the report name to [a-z0-9-], caps it at 60 chars, and appends the UTC date. That slug is what keeps a user-supplied name out of the Content-Disposition header and off the filesystem — the download handler relies on it and does no escaping of its own.
RenderAll stops at the first failure: a delivery carrying only some of the configured files is not the report the client configured.
